Capability Unit IVe-3 Dryland
This unit consists of moderately deep and deep sloping and rolling soils. Their texture ranges from fine sandy loam to clay. They are well drained and range in permeability from rapid to slow. They occur on floodplains, terraces, fans, footslopes, and shale and sandstone highlands. The available water holding capacity is 5 to 12 inches. Runoff is medium.
The frost free season is 105 to 125 days. The annual precipitation is 12 to 14 inches.
There is a moderate risk of soil blowing on the soils with clay, silt loam and fine sandy loam surface textures. The deep and moderately deep soils are suitable for dryland small grain crops only with adequate erosion control and diversion of runoff from overlying soils. Severe gullying will occur where runoff collects in drainageways unless they are in permanent sod. The main use of these soils is pasture, hayland and range. Bromegrass, alfalfa, crested wheatgrass and pubescent wheatgrass are suitable species for hay and pasture planting.
Capability Unit IVs-2 Dryland
This unit consists of shallow, moderately deep and deep, nearly level to sloping soils on terraces, fans, floodplains, and shale highlands. Texture ranges from loam and gravelly loam to clay. The soils are well drained except for the Haverson and Lohmiller soils, and the Saline land which bore a seasonal water table and salts within a 5-foot depth. Permeability ranges from very slow to rapid. The available water holding capacity is 4 to 13 inches. Runoff is slow to medium.
The frost free season is 100 to 125 days. The annual precipitation if 11 to 14 inches.
Soils in this unit have a slight to moderate water erosion hazard.
The soils in the unit are suited for range and dryland small grains. The Saline land and the saline Haverson, Bone and Lohmiller soils are suited to salt tolerant grasses such as tall wheatgrass. The Allentine, Pierre, and Kyle soils are hard when dry and very sticky and plastic when wet. They have a narrow moisture range at which they can be easily tilled.
Grass species suitable for planting on these soils are bromegrass, crested wheatgrass, Siberian wheatgrass, green needlegrass, and pubescent wheatgrass.
Capability Unit VIe
This unit consists of shallow, moderately deep, and deep soils on valley bottoms, terraces, loess covered hills, and shale, sandstone and limestone plains.
